scope: Magnitude and definition screening; no parameter fitting, clipping or biological validation.

references.title: Individual Muscle Contributions to the Acceleration of the Center of Mass During the Barbell Back Squat in Trained Female Subjects
references.protocol: 13 trained women; parallel back squat at 85% 1RM; reported right side; static-optimization estimates.
references.comparison_limits: Different participants, load and motion. Ratios below are descriptive, not prediction errors or acceptance intervals. Do not add separately timed peaks.

references.title: Muscle Force Dynamics Across Increasing Squat Intensity Conditions in Elite Powerlifters
references.locator: Abstract; numerical full-text force curves not extracted in this review
references.notes: 29 powerlifters at 70-90% 1RM. Vasti had the largest absolute forces; increasing intensity did not uniformly increase every muscle in the sticking region.

references.title: Movement Strategies for Countermovement Jumping are Potentially Influenced by Elastic Energy Stored and Released from Tendons
references.locator: Results: joint kinetics; Methods: data analysis
references.protocol: 16 men, 74.2 +/- 5.8 kg; hands at vest; CMJ with varied height or added vest mass. Right-leg inverse dynamics.
references.force_method: Ankle moment divided by model Achilles moment arm; not direct tendon-force measurement.
references.comparison_limits: Our gastrocnemius+soleus scalar tension sum is a related proxy, not the same single tendon resultant; other plantarflexors and antagonism differ.

references.title: Force-length-velocity behavior and muscle-specific joint moment contributions during countermovement and squat jumps
references.notes: Eight basketball players; static-optimization CMJ/SJ estimates. Muscle force differences depended on length-velocity behavior even with similar GRF and jump height. No absolute-force threshold extracted here.

references.title: Biomechanical analysis of hip, knee, and ankle joint contact forces during squats in elite powerlifters
references.notes: 29 elite lifters, 70-90% 1RM. At 90%, estimated peak resultants: hip 15.5, tibiofemoral 23.2, patellofemoral 26.7, ankle 11.5 BW. This is model estimation at heavy loads, not direct validation of our joint forces. Thigh-calf contact was omitted.
